title: Refactor Workflow Modules into a Three-Layer Architecture

story.so_that: I can add new workflows by creating a package and registering it in the orchestrator catalog without modifying existing workflow code or entangling generic infrastructure with domain behavior
story.i_want: to refactor the orchestrator package into three layers (common, orchestrator, and workflow modules) with a stable module contract

journey.before: Taylor needs to add or modify a workflow, but the orchestrator package mixes generic Cadence/Devin infrastructure, Story Analysis behavior, and Worker startup, making changes risky and entangled. Different affected users include Story Analysis workflow maintainers, new workflow authors, and operators who start and stop Workers.
journey.during: Taylor refactors the codebase into three layers: common owns generic infrastructure, each workflow package owns its complete domain, and orchestrator is the composition root that loads configured modules.
journey.after: Taylor adds a new workflow by creating a package and a catalog entry; the orchestrator mounts it on its own task list without touching existing workflow code.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Refactor the existing orchestrator package into a three-layer architecture (common infrastructure, workflow packages, and orchestrator composition root), define a WorkflowModuleSpec contract, and make the orchestrator load configured Python module paths and run one Cadence Worker per domain/task-list pair.
inputs: Current orchestrator package source code and package layout
Existing Story Analysis workflow implementation, activities, and tests
Cadence Python SDK and Worker/Registry APIs
Start/stop scripts and domain registration scripts
outputs: New src/common/ package with workflow-agnostic interfaces and infrastructure
New or populated src/story_analysis_workflow/ package owning complete Story Analysis behavior
Refactored src/orchestrator/ package as the composition root
Updated start/stop scripts for multi-Worker startup and shutdown
Moved and updated tests for common, workflow-module, and orchestrator
Validated dependency rules and live Cadence integration
state_changes: Generic infrastructure moves from orchestrator/ into common/
Story Analysis domain code moves from orchestrator/ into story_analysis_workflow/
orchestrator/ becomes the application composition root that imports common and configured workflow module entry points
Dependency direction becomes common <- workflow modules <- orchestrator
Orchestrator loads configured Python module paths and groups them by (domain, task_list)
One Cadence Worker is created and supervised per domain/task-list pair
Stale Story Analysis code and imports are removed from orchestrator/

acceptance_criteria.criterion: common contains generic interfaces and infrastructure and imports no workflow package or orchestrator module
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the common package is created When its imports are analyzed Then it contains no references to orchestrator or any workflow package

acceptance_criteria.criterion: each workflow package imports generic capabilities from common and never imports another workflow package
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow package exists When its imports are analyzed Then it imports only common and its own modules

acceptance_criteria.criterion: story_analysis_workflow owns its workflow definition, engine, contracts, complete Activity folder, domain logic, clients, configuration, and tests
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the refactor is complete When the story_analysis_workflow package is inspected Then it contains all Story Analysis-specific workflow, engine, activity, contract, and client code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: orchestrator imports common and configured workflow module entry points as the application composition root
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the orchestrator package is built When its dependencies are inspected Then it imports only common and the configured workflow module entry points

acceptance_criteria.criterion: orchestrator contains no Story Analysis skill names, grading rules, artifact conventions, Activity implementations, or result details
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the orchestrator package is refactored When its source is searched for Story Analysis domain concepts Then no skill names, grading rules, artifact conventions, Activity implementations, or result details remain
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Remove domain knowledge from the composition root

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the orchestrator loads supported workflow modules from configured Python module paths
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow catalog configuration exists When the orchestrator starts Then it imports each configured Python module path and validates its SPEC

acceptance_criteria.criterion: each workflow module declares its domain, task list, workflow names, Activity names, and registration callable
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow package is configured When its module descriptor is inspected Then it exposes name, domain, task_list, workflow_types, activity_types, and a register callable

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the orchestrator validates registrations and creates one Cadence Worker per domain/task-list pair
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given configured workflow module specs When the orchestrator composes Workers Then it groups modules by (domain, task_list), detects conflicts, and creates one Worker per group
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Run independent Workers per task list

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the start script registers all configured domains and waits for every configured Worker to poll
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the start-workflow-engine script runs When it starts the orchestrator Then it registers every configured domain and waits until all Workers report polling

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the stop path shuts down every Worker cleanly
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the stop script runs When it shuts down the orchestrator Then every Worker context is cancelled and closed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: generic logging identifies workflow modules and task-list-specific Workers without assuming a Story Analysis module name
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the logging implementation is moved to common When logs are emitted Then they include domain and task_list but do not hard-code story-analysis references

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the single-Activity diagnostic workflow remains top-level and can target Activities on each mounted task list, or its unresolved routing behavior is captured in an approved follow-up before the old path is removed
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the single-Activity diagnostic workflow is implemented When it is invoked Then it can target Activities on each mounted task list or its unresolved routing is documented and approved before removal

acceptance_criteria.criterion: a second workflow is mounted by adding its package and orchestrator catalog entry, without changing Story Analysis code
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a new workflow package exists When it is added to the orchestrator catalog Then Story Analysis code is unchanged and the new workflow runs independently
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Add workflows without modifying existing ones

acceptance_criteria.criterion: all common, workflow-module, orchestrator, and live Cadence integration tests pass
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the refactor is complete When the test suites and integration tests run Then all common, workflow-module, orchestrator, and live Cadence tests pass

acceptance_criteria.criterion: stale Story Analysis implementations and imports are removed from orchestrator after migration
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the migration is complete When the orchestrator package is inspected Then no stale Story Analysis implementations or imports remain

acceptance_criteria.criterion: a second workflow is mounted and both it and Story Analysis run on independent Workers without code changes
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a second workflow package and catalog entry exist When the orchestrator starts and a representative workflow run is started Then both Workers poll and the new workflow executes without modifying Story Analysis files
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Add a new workflow without side effects

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the orchestrator fails fast when a configured module path is missing or invalid
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow catalog contains an unimportable or invalid module path When the orchestrator starts Then it raises a startup error and creates no Workers
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Detect bad configuration before Workers are created

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the orchestrator handles an empty workflow catalog gracefully
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the workflow catalog contains no module paths When the orchestrator composes Workers Then it reports zero configured Workers and does not crash

acceptance_criteria.criterion: workflow module dependency violations are detected and rejected
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow module descriptor or source imports another workflow package or the orchestrator When it is loaded Then validation or static checks fail the module

edge_cases.gherkin: Given the orchestrator workflow catalog is empty When the orchestrator starts Then it reports no configured Workers and exits or idles cleanly

edge_cases.criterion: Missing or unimportable configured module path
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a catalog entry points to a non-existent or unimportable Python module When the orchestrator loads it Then it raises a clear import error before creating any Worker
edge_cases.jtbd: Fail fast on a bad module path

edge_cases.gherkin: Given a configured module exists but does not define a valid `SPEC` When the orchestrator validates it Then it raises a validation error

edge_cases.criterion: Duplicate module names or duplicate workflow/Activity wire names
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the catalog contains two modules with the same name or overlapping wire names within a Worker registry When the orchestrator composes the registry Then it detects the conflict and fails startup

edge_cases.criterion: Two modules configured for the same domain and task list
edge_cases.gherkin: Given two modules declare the same domain and task list When the orchestrator groups them Then they share one Worker if names do not conflict, or fail if they do

edge_cases.criterion: Module descriptor with empty required fields
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a module `SPEC` has an empty name, domain, or task_list When the orchestrator validates it Then it rejects the descriptor
Given the Cadence server is not reachable When the orchestrator creates a Worker Then startup fails with a clear domain or client error

edge_cases.criterion: Partial Worker failure in a multi-Worker process
edge_cases.gherkin: Given one of several Workers fails to start or crashes When the orchestrator is running Then it cancels remaining Workers and reports the failure

edge_cases.criterion: Single-Activity diagnostic workflow without resolved task-list routing
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the diagnostic workflow is started and no routing design has been chosen When it executes Then it does not silently schedule on the wrong task list and the open behavior is documented

edge_cases.criterion: Workflow module that imports another workflow package or orchestrator
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a workflow module source or descriptor imports a disallowed package When dependency checks run Then the violation is caught before the module is mounted
edge_cases.jtbd: Enforce dependency direction at load time

questions.question: How will SingleActivityWorkflow route its Activity to the correct task list when workflow modules are isolated?
Should multiple Cadence Workers share one Python process or run in separate subprocesses?
Does the installed Cadence Python SDK support registry-bound workflow registration after class definition?
How should the Story Analysis-specific skill output-path fallback be handled while the general resolution refactor is deferred?
What is the exact format, versioning, and ownership of workflow_catalog.json?
How will the orchestrator detect, report, and clean up a failed Worker in a multi-Worker process?
Should an empty workflow catalog be an error, a warning, or an idle process?

infrastructure: Local Cadence server with domain registration
